effect: Defines the APOE e4 allele together with rs7412 (e4 = C at rs429358 plus C at rs7412). Each copy of C at rs429358 is part of the e4 (or rare e1) haplotype, associated with higher late-onset Alzheimer's disease risk.
strand: + strand, GRCh37: T/C. APOE lies on the + strand, so the C allele is also the gene-strand allele. Combine with rs7412 to get the haplotype (see the APOE section of the report).
notes: Informational only, not medical advice. Do not interpret in isolation: use the APOE haplotype. dbSNP: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/rs429358

genotypes.TT: No C allele: no e4 (or e1) haplotype from this SNP.
genotypes.CT: One C allele: one e4 (or rare e1) haplotype; confirm with rs7412.
genotypes.CC: Two C alleles: two e4 (or rare e1) haplotypes; confirm with rs7412.

effect: Defines the APOE e2 allele together with rs429358 (e2 = T at rs429358 plus T at rs7412). The T allele marks e2 (or rare e1) and is associated with lower Alzheimer's risk but possible type III hyperlipoproteinemia.
strand: + strand, GRCh37: C/T. APOE lies on the + strand, so the T allele is also the gene-strand allele.
notes: Informational only, not medical advice. Use together with rs429358. dbSNP: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/rs7412

genotypes.CC: No T allele: no e2 (or e1) haplotype from this SNP.
genotypes.CT: One T allele: one e2 (or rare e1) haplotype; confirm with rs429358.
genotypes.TT: Two T alleles: two e2 (or rare e1) haplotypes; confirm with rs429358.

effect: MTHFR C677T (A222V). The variant allele reduces MTHFR enzyme activity; the clinical impact is modest and depends on folate status.
strand: Reported on the + strand (GRCh37) as G/A. MTHFR is on the - strand, so the commonly named 677T variant (gene strand, C>T) appears as A on the + strand. Risk allele here = A (+ strand) = T (gene strand).
notes: Informational only, not medical advice. Many labs report this SNP on the gene strand (C/T); check the strand before comparing. dbSNP: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/rs1801133

genotypes.GG: No copies of 677T (gene-strand notation 677CC): typical enzyme activity.
genotypes.AG: One copy of 677T (heterozygous, 677CT): mildly reduced enzyme activity in some studies.
genotypes.AA: Two copies of 677T (homozygous, 677TT): reduced enzyme activity (roughly a third of typical in vitro); health impact is modest and context dependent.

strand: Reported on the + strand (GRCh37) as T/G. MTHFR is on the - strand, so the named 1298C variant (gene strand, A>C) appears as G on the + strand. Risk allele here = G (+ strand) = C (gene strand). Verify the strand against your data source.
notes: Informational only, not medical advice. dbSNP: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/rs1801131

genotypes.GG: Two copies of 1298C (homozygous, 1298CC): mildly reduced enzyme activity.

effect: Factor V Leiden (R506Q). The variant allele causes activated protein C resistance and raises the risk of venous thrombosis.
strand: Reported on the + strand (GRCh37) as C/T. F5 is on the - strand, so the Factor V Leiden change (gene strand G>A) appears as T on the + strand. Risk allele here = T (+ strand) = A (gene strand). Note: the GRCh37 reference base at this site is T (the Leiden allele) while GRCh38 has C, so on a GRCh37 variant-only VCF an absent site would be inferred TT; treat any inferred call here with extra caution.
notes: Informational only, not medical advice. A positive result should be confirmed by a clinical test and discussed with a clinician. dbSNP: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/rs6025

genotypes.CT: Heterozygous Factor V Leiden: venous thrombosis risk is increased several-fold over baseline (estimates vary).
genotypes.TT: Homozygous Factor V Leiden: much higher relative venous thrombosis risk (estimates vary widely); seek clinical advice.

effect: HFE C282Y. Homozygosity is the main cause of HFE hereditary hemochromatosis (iron overload), with incomplete penetrance.
strand: Reported on the + strand (GRCh37) as G/A. HFE is on the + strand, so the A allele is also the gene-strand allele (c.845G>A, p.Cys282Tyr).
notes: Informational only, not medical advice. Confirm with clinical testing (ferritin, transferrin saturation). dbSNP: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/rs1800562

genotypes.AG: One C282Y allele (carrier): usually no iron overload on its own.
genotypes.AA: Two C282Y alleles: at risk of HFE hemochromatosis; penetrance is incomplete, seek clinical advice.

effect: LCT -13910 C/T. The T allele (gene strand) is the lactase persistence allele in European-ancestry populations. This is a trait, not a disease risk.
strand: Reported on the + strand (GRCh37) as G/A. The gene-strand -13910*C (non-persistent) and *T (persistent) appear as G and A respectively on the + strand. Risk (persistence) allele here = A (+ strand) = T (gene strand).
notes: Informational only. Other variants cause lactase persistence in other populations, so GG does not guarantee lactose intolerance. dbSNP: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/rs4988235

genotypes.GG: Two non-persistence alleles (gene strand CC): lactase activity likely declines in adulthood in European-ancestry people.
genotypes.AG: One persistence allele (gene strand CT): lactase persistence is typically dominant, so likely persistent.
genotypes.AA: Two persistence alleles (gene strand TT): lactase persistence.
